content.comment_body: Hello, I'm working with a [product_name] [article_no] and have enabled web server access. The running program contains message texts, and several are visible directly on the device's screen. However, when I log in using a web browser, nothing appears. Neither the BM-style nor the TDE-style browser views show any content; I only see blank screens for both. I have tested this with IE11 and Chrome (v38). What could be causing this issue?

Hello. Based on your description, it might be related to how the program was configured. Could you share a segment of your program? The initial thing to check is whether the messages are properly activated (they should have an ON signal at the block's input). Also, confirm that the web server selector within the [product_name] instructions is enabled. It’s possible you have everything set up and the program is fully loaded, but without seeing a sample program, we can’t be certain. For reference, we use Firefox, but browser choice shouldn’t impact this. Regards.
Did you enable the option for message texts to be displayed specifically for the Web Server?
That solved it. I had overlooked that new checkbox. This program was previously running on a different [product_name] version. Thanks a lot.

analysis.insight_summary: Users experienced difficulty viewing configured message texts on the web interface of a [product_name] [article_no], even though these messages were shown on the device screen and web server access was enabled. The issue stemmed from a separate setting that needed to be activated to display message texts on the web server, which was different from previous versions. Users assumed configurations from older hardware would transfer automatically and expected features to be enabled across all platforms without extra steps.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect message texts to be displayed in the web browser interface (BM and TDE styles) just as they appear on the device screen, and expect that migrating their program from an older [product_name] module would not require any additional settings.
